rationale:
The example `requirements.sdk.graph.hierarchical-paths` gives a concrete case. A Habeas-style `NodeId` enum has a `Requirement(Vec<String>)` variant holding the dotted path `a.b.c`. `node_path` must turn it into `["requirement", "a", "b", "c"]`. The example cites `requirements.sdk.graph.node_path_method`, which requires the mapping to be 1:1 and stable.

The only {test} reference is `crates/habeas-sdk/tests/contracts.rs#fn[hierarchical_requirement_identity_maps_each_component_to_a_path_segment]`. It defines the same illustrative `HabeasNodeId` enum and a `node_path` mapping that prepends "requirement" to the components. It builds `Requirement(["a","b","c"])` and asserts the resulting `NodePath.segments` equal `["requirement","a","b","c"]`. That covers the stated expected output, including each dotted component becoming its own segment. It also asserts that converting the same id twice gives equal paths, which covers the determinism part of the cited requirement.

The test uses a local mapping because the example describes a domain-defined conversion that Habeas "might define". The SDK owns no such conversion for the test to call. The SDK-level `node_path` contract is tested elsewhere: `fn[identities_remain_stable_and_fingerprinting_uses_the_supplied_snapshot]` carries the `node_path_method` {test} reference. It checks stability across content changes and across graph instances, and it checks that distinct nodes get distinct paths. That test is cited context, so I did not reassess it.

I found no outcome in the example that the test fails to check.
